title: Suraqah's Pursuit
reader_question: How did the horseman who rode out to capture the Prophet ﷺ end up turning his pursuers away?

overview.text: Quraysh had not let the Prophet ﷺ go. Their messengers went out to the tribes with an offer: the blood-money of each man, for the Prophet ﷺ and for Abu Bakr, to whoever killed or captured him. Among Banu Mudlij, Suraqah ibn Malik heard it, and he hoped to win it. So when a man of his tribe walked into their gathering saying he had seen riders by the coast, Suraqah knew at once who they were, and told no one. What happened when he caught up with them, he told afterwards in his own words.

Abu Bakr remembered the horse sinking to its belly, and Suraqah leaping clear of it. "Muhammad, I know this is your doing," Suraqah said. paragraphs.text: Ibn Ishaq's telling, like al-Bukhari's, goes back to Suraqah himself, but the two differ in their details. In al-Bukhari, Quraysh offer the blood-money of each man for killing or capturing him; Suraqah's horse stumbles once, he casts the arrows, rides on, and then its forelegs sink; ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah writes the letter on leather. In Ibn Ishaq, and in the same story as Musa ibn ‘Uqbah heard it from al-Zuhri, the price is a hundred she-camels for bringing the Prophet ﷺ back; Suraqah puts on his armour and casts the arrows before he sets out ("He will not harm him"); the horse stumbles twice and he falls each time, asking "What is this?"; at the third fall its forelegs go into the ground; and Abu Bakr writes the letter, on a bone, a scrap or a potsherd. The story above follows al-Bukhari and names Ibn Ishaq where his version adds or differs.

in_depth.title: Abu Bakr's side of the story

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr told his part to ‘Azib, al-Bara's father, who would not let him take home a saddle he had bought until he told how he and the Prophet ﷺ had fared on the road with the idolaters searching for them. Al-Bara heard it, and al-Bayhaqi notes that al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it. The two men saw the same moments from opposite ends: Suraqah tells of his arrows and his own change of heart; Abu Bakr of his fear, the Prophet's ﷺ prayer, and Suraqah's plea for a prayer in return. Suraqah says the forelegs sank to the knees; Abu Bakr says the horse sank to its belly.

لَمَّا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ مِنْ مَكَّةَ مُهَاجِرًا إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، جَعَلَتْ قُرَيْش فِيهِ مائَة نَاقَةٍ لِمَنْ رَدَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ. قَالَ: فَبَيْنَا أَنَا جَالِسٌ فِي نَادِي قَوْمِي إذْ أَقْبَلَ رَجُلٌ مِنَّا، حَتَّى وَقَفَ عَلَيْنَا، فَقَالَ: وَاَللَّهِ لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ رَكْبَهُ ثَلَاثَةً مَرُّوا عَلَيَّ آنِفًا، إنِّي لَأَرَاهُمْ مُحَمَّدًا وَأَصْحَابَهُ، قَالَ: فَأَوْمَأْتُ إلَيْهِ بِعَيْنِي: أَنْ اُسْكُتْ، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: إنَّمَا هُمْ بَنُو فُلَانٍ، يَبْتَغُونَ ضَالَّةً لَهُمْ، قَالَ: لَعَلَّهُ، ثُمَّ سَكَتَ. قَالَ: ثُمَّ مَكَثْتُ قَلِيلًا، ثُمَّ قُمْتُ فَدَخَلْتُ بَيْتِي، ثُمَّ أَمَرْتُ بِفَرَسِي، فَقُيِّدَ لِي إلَى بَطْنِ الْوَادِي، وَأَمَرْتُ بِسِلَاحِي، فَأُخْرِجَ لِي مِنْ دُبُرِ حُجْرَتِي، ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُ قِدَاحِي الَّتِي أَسَتَقْسِمُ بِهَا، ثُمَّ انْطَلَقْتُ، فَلَبِسْتُ لَأْمَتِي [٢]، ثُمَّ أَخَرَجْتُ قِدَاحِي، فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِهَا، فَخَرَجَ السَّهْمُ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ «لَا يَضُرُّهُ» [٣] .
قَالَ: وَكُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ أَرُدَّهُ عَلَى قُرَيْش، فآخذ الْمِائَة النَّاقَةِ. قَالَ: فَرَكِبْتُ عَلَى أَثَرِهِ، فَبَيْنَمَا فَرَسِي يَشْتَدُّ بِي عَثَرَ بِي، فَسَقَطْتُ عَنْهُ. قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: مَا هَذَا؟ قَالَ:
ثُمَّ أَخَرَجْتُ قِدَاحِي فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِهَا، فَخَرَجَ السَّهْمُ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ «لَا يَضُرُّهُ» . قَالَ:
فَأَبَيْتُ إلَّا أَنْ أَتَّبِعَهُ. قَالَ: فَرَكِبْتُ فِي أَثَرِهِ، فَبَيْنَا فَرَسِي يَشْتَدُّ بِي، عَثَرَ بِي، فَسَقَطْتُ عَنْهُ. قَالَ: فَقُلْتُ: مَا هَذَا؟، قَالَ: ثُمَّ أَخَرَجْتُ قِدَاحِي فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِهَا فَخَرَجَ السَّهْمُ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ «لَا يَضُرُّهُ»، قَالَ: فَأَبَيْتُ إلَّا أَنْ أَتَّبِعَهُ، فَرَكِبْتُ فِي أَثَرِهِ.
فَلَمَّا بَدَا لِي الْقَوْمُ وَرَأَيْتهمْ، عَثَرَ بِي فَرَسِي، فَذَهَبَتْ يَدَاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ، وَسَقَطْتُ عَنْهُ، ثُمَّ انْتَزَعَ يَدَيْهِ مِنْ الْأَرْضِ، وَتَبِعَهُمَا دُخَانٌ كَالْإِعْصَارِ [٤] . قَالَ: فَعَرَفْتُ حَيْنَ رَأَيْتُ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ مُنِعَ مِنِّي، وَأَنَّهُ ظَاهِرٌ. قَالَ: فَنَادَيْتُ الْقَوْمَ: فَقُلْتُ: أَنَا سُرَاقَةُ بْنُ جُعْشُمٍ: انظرونى أكلمكم، فو الله لَا أَرَيْبُكُمْ، وَلَا يَأْتِيكُمْ مِنِّي شَيْءٌ
source_units.text:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Makkah, migrating to Madinah, Quraysh offered one hundred she-camels for whoever brought him back to them. He said: As I sat in my people’s gathering, one of our men came and stood before us. He said, “By Allah, I just saw a party of three pass me; I think they are Muhammad and his companions.” I signaled with my eyes for him to be quiet, then said, “They are only members of such-and-such a family looking for something of theirs that they had lost.” He said, “Perhaps so,” and fell silent. He said: I waited a little, then got up and entered my house. I ordered my horse to be tethered for me in the valley bottom and my weapons to be brought out behind my dwelling. I took the arrows with which I drew lots, set out, put on my armor [٢], then brought out my arrows and drew lots. The arrow I disliked came out: “He will not harm him” [٣].
He said: I hoped to bring him back to Quraysh and take the hundred she-camels. I rode in pursuit of him; as my horse galloped with me, it stumbled and I fell. I said, “What is this?” He said:
Then I brought out my arrows and drew lots. The arrow I disliked came out: “He will not harm him.” He said:
I insisted on following him. I rode after him, and while my horse galloped with me it stumbled and I fell. I said, “What is this?” He said: Then I brought out my arrows and drew lots, and the arrow I disliked came out: “He will not harm him.” He said: I insisted on following him and rode after him.
When the people came into view and I saw them, my horse stumbled, its forelegs went into the ground, and I fell off. Then it pulled its forelegs out of the ground, followed by smoke like a whirlwind [٤]. He said: When I saw that, I knew he had been protected from me and that he would prevail. I called to the people: “I am Suraqa ibn Ju‘shum. Wait for me so I can speak to you. By Allah, I will cause you no alarm, nor will anything come from me that you

source_units.text_ar: فَعَثَرَتْ بِي فَرَسِي، فَخَرَرْتُ عَنْهَا، فَقُمْتُ فَأَهْوَيْتُ يَدِي إِلَى كِنَانَتِي، فَاسْتَخْرَجْتُ مِنْهَا الْأَزْلَامَ فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِهَا: أَضُرُّهُمْ أَمْ لَا، فَخَرَجَ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ، فَرَكِبْتُ فَرَسِي، وَعَصَيْتُ الْأَزْلَامَ، تُقَرَِّبُ بِي حَتَّى إِذَا سَمِعْتُ قِرَاءَةَ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ وَهْوَ لَا يَلْتَفِتُ، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ يُكْثِرُ الِالْتِفَاتَ،
source_units.text: when my horse stumbled and I fell off. I got up, reached into my quiver, took out the divining arrows, and drew lots with them: should I harm them or not? The result was the one I disliked. I mounted my horse, defied the divining arrows, and it carried me closer until I could hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting. He did not look back, while Abu Bakr kept looking back,

source_units.text_ar: فَارْتَحَلْنَا بَعْدَ مَا زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ، وَاتَّبَعَنَا سُرَاقَةُ بْنُ مَالِكِ، قَالَ: وَنَحْنُ فِي جَلَدٍ [(٤)] مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه أُتِينَا، فَقَالَ
source_units.text: We set out after the sun had passed its zenith, and Suraqa ibn Malik followed us. He said: We were on firm ground [(٤)], and I said, “Messenger of Allah, we have been overtaken!” He said:

source_units.text_ar: لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّه مَعَنَا»،
source_units.kind_ar: كلام النبي في خبر أبي بكر
source_units.speaker_ar: النبي ﷺ في خبر أبي بكر
source_units.text: “Do not grieve; Allah is with us.”

source_units.text_ar:
﵌ إِدَاوَةً عَلَى فَمِهَا خِرْقَةٌ، فَصَبَبْتُ عَلَى اللَّبَنِ حَتَّى بَرُدَ أَسْفَلُهُ، فَأَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّه ﵌، فَوَافَقْتُهُ وَقَدِ اسْتَيْقَظَ، فَقُلْتُ: أَتَشْرَبُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه؟ فَشَرِبَ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌، حَتَّى رَضِيتُ، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: قَدْ آنَ الرَّحِيلُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه.
قَالَ: فَارْتَحَلْنَا وَالْقَوْمُ يَطْلُبُونَنَا، فَلَمْ يُدْرِكْنَا أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ غَيْرُ سُرَاقَةَ بن مالك ابن جُعْشُمٍ عَلَى فَرَسٍ لَهُ فَقُلْتُ هَذَا الطَّلَبُ قَدْ لَحِقَنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه، قَالَ: لَا تَحْزَنْ، إِنَّ اللَّه مَعَنَا، فَلَمَّا أَنْ دَنَا مِنَّا وَكَانَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُ قِيدَ رُمْحَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثَةٍ، قُلْتُ: هَذَا الطَّلَبُ قَدْ لَحِقَنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه، وَبَكَيْتُ، فَقَالَ: مَا يُبْكِيكَ؟
فَقُلْتُ: أَمَا واللَّه مَا عَلَى نَفْسِي أَبْكِي، وَلَكِنِّي إِنَّمَا أَبْكِي عَلَيْكَ، قَالَ: فَدَعَا عَلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌ فَقَالَ: اللهُمَّ! اكْفِنَا بِمَا شِئْتَ، قَالَ: فَسَاخَتْ بِهِ فَرَسُهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَى بَطْنِهَا، فَوَثَبَ عَنْهَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ هَذَا عَمَلُكَ فَادْعُ اللَّه أَنْ تُنَجِيَنِي مِمَّا أَنَا فِيهِ، فو اللَّه لَأُعَمِّيَنَّ عَلَى مَنْ وَرَائِي مِنَ الطَّلَبِ، وَهَذِهِ كِنَانَتِي فَخُذْ مِنْهَا سَهْمًا، فَإِنَّكَ سَتَمُرُّ بِإِبِلِي وَغَنَمِي بِمَكَانِ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَخُذْ مِنْهَا حَاجَتَكَ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌: لَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا فِي إِبِلِكَ وَغَنَمِكَ، وَدَعَا لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌، فَانْطَلَقَ رَاجِعًا إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ، وَمَضَى رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌، وَأَنَا مَعَهُ حَتَّى قَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ لَيْلًا» [(٢)] .
source_units.text: He said: ‘We set out while the people were pursuing us, but none of them caught up with us except Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum, riding his horse. I said, “The pursuers have caught up with us, Messenger of Allah!” He said, “Do not grieve; Allah is with us.” When Suraqah drew near, and there were only two or three spear-lengths between us, I said, “The pursuers have caught up with us, Messenger of Allah!” and I wept. He said, “What makes you weep?” I replied, “By Allah, I am not weeping for myself; I am weeping only for you.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed against him, saying, “O Allah, protect us from him in whatever way You will.” Suraqah’s horse sank into the ground up to its belly. He jumped off it and said, “Muhammad, I know this is your doing. Pray to Allah to rescue me from this predicament, and by Allah, I will turn away the pursuers behind me. Here is my quiver; take an arrow from it. You will pass by my camels and sheep at such-and-such a place, so take what you need from them.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “We have no need of your camels or sheep.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for him, and Suraqah went back to his companions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I continued until we arrived in Madinah at night.’

source_units.text_ar: سَاخَتْ يَدَا فَرَسِي فِي الْأَرْضِ، حَتَّى بَلَغَتَا الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ، فَخَرَرْتُ عَنْهَا، ثُمَّ زَجَرْتُهَا فَنَهَضَتْ، فَلَمْ تَكَدْ تُخْرِجُ يَدَيْهَا، فَلَمَّا اسْتَوَتْ قَائِمَةً، إِذَا لِأَثَرِ يَدَيْهَا عُثَانٌ سَاطِعٌ فِي السَّمَاءِ مِثْلُ الدُّخَانِ، فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِالْأَزْلَامِ، فَخَرَجَ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ، فَنَادَيْتُهُمْ بِالْأَمَانِ فَوَقَفُوا، فَرَكِبْتُ فَرَسِي حَتَّى جِئْتُهُمْ، وَوَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِي حِينَ لَقِيتُ مَا لَقِيتُ مِنَ الْحَبْسِ عَنْهُمْ، أَنْ سَيَظْهَرُ أَمْرُ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ. فَقُلْتُ لَهُ: إِنَّ قَوْمَكَ قَدْ جَعَلُوا فِيكَ الدِّيَةَ، وَأَخْبَرْتُهُمْ أَخْبَارَ مَا يُرِيدُ النَّاسُ بِهِمْ، وَعَرَضْتُ عَلَيْهِمِ الزَّادَ وَالْمَتَاعَ، فَلَمْ يَرْزَآنِي وَلَمْ يَسْأَلَانِي، إِلَّا أَنْ قَالَ:
source_units.text: when my horse’s forelegs sank into the earth as far as the knees, and I fell off. I urged it on and it rose, scarcely able to pull its forelegs out. Once it stood upright, dust rose from the traces of its forelegs into the sky like smoke. I drew lots with the divining arrows, and the result was the one I disliked. I called to them asking for safe conduct, and they stopped. I mounted and came to them. When I experienced being held back from reaching them, it occurred to me that the cause of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would prevail. I said to him, ‘Your people have offered the blood-money for you.’ I told them what people intended for them and offered them provisions and goods. They took nothing from me and asked nothing of me, except that he said:

source_units.text_ar: أَخْفِ عَنَّا
source_units.text: “Keep our whereabouts hidden.”

source_units.text_ar: فَسَأَلْتُهُ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ لِي كِتَابَ أَمْنٍ، فَأَمَرَ عَامِرَ بْنَ فُهَيْرَةَ فَكَتَبَ فِي رُقْعَةٍ مِنْ أَدِيمٍ، ثُمَّ مَضَى رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ.
source_units.text: I asked him to have a letter of safety written for me. He instructed Amir ibn Fuhayrah, who wrote it on a piece of leather. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on his way.

source_units.text_ar: هَذَا الطُّلَّبُ أَيِ الطَّالِبُ يَقَعُ عَلَى الْوَاحِدِ وَالْجَمْعِ فَسَاخَتْ فَرَسُهُ أَيْ دَخَلَ يَدَاهَا وَرِجْلَاهَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لَأُعَمِيَنَّ لَأُخْفِيَنَّ
source_units.text: This al-tullab (الطُّلَّبُ), meaning al-talib (الطَّالِبُ), can apply to one or to several. “His horse sank” means its forelegs and hind legs entered the earth. “I shall obscure” means “I shall conceal.”

source_units.text_ar: تَكْرَهُونَهُ. قَالَ: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ:
source_units.text: dislike.” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr:

source_units.text_ar: قُلْ لَهُ: وَمَا تَبْتَغِي مِنَّا؟
source_units.text: “Ask him: What do you want from us?”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ: فَقَالَ ذَلِكَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، قَالَ: قُلْتُ: تَكْتُبُ لِي كِتَابًا يَكُونُ آيَةً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ. قَالَ:
source_units.text: He said: Abu Bakr said that. I said, “Write me a letter that will serve as a sign between you and me.” He said:

source_units.text_ar: اُكْتُبْ لَهُ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ.
source_units.text: “Write it for him, Abu Bakr.”

source_units.text_ar: (قَالَ) [١]: فَكَتَبَ لِي كِتَابًا فِي عَظْمٍ، أَوْ فِي رُقْعَةٍ، أَوْ فِي خَزَفَةٍ، ثُمَّ أَلْقَاهُ إلَيَّ، فَأَخَذَتْهُ، فَجَعَلْتُهُ فِي كِنَانَتِي، ثُمَّ رَجَعْتُ [٢]، فَسَكَتُّ فَلَمْ أَذْكُرْ شَيْئًا مِمَّا كَانَ
source_units.text: (He said) [١]: He wrote me a letter on a bone, or a scrap, or a potsherd, then tossed it to me. I took it and placed it in my quiver, then went back [٢]. I kept silent and mentioned nothing of what had

source_units.text_ar:
فَدَعَا عَلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌ فَارْتَطَمَتْ فَرَسُهُ إِلَى بَطْنِهَا [(٥)]
فَقَالَ:
source_units.kind_ar: خبر أبي بكر: الدعاء وسوخ الفرس
source_units.text:
The Messenger of Allah ﵌ prayed against him, and his horse sank into the ground up to its belly [(٥)].
Then he said:

source_units.text_ar: إِنِّي قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكُمَا قَدْ دَعَوْتُمَا عَلَيَّ فَادْعُوَا لِي، فَاللهُ لَكُمَا أَنْ أَرُدَّ عَنْكُمَا الطَّلَبَ،
source_units.text: “I know that you two have prayed against me, so pray for me. Allah is my witness to you both that I will turn the pursuers back from you.”

source_units.text_ar: فَدَعَا اللَّه فَنَجَا، فَرَجَعَ لَا يَلْقَى أَحَدًا إِلَّا قَالَ:
source_units.kind_ar: خبر أبي بكر: نجاة سراقة ورجوعه
source_units.text: He prayed to Allah and Suraqa was saved. He went back and said to everyone he met:

source_units.text_ar: قَدْ كُفِيتُمْ مَا هَهُنَا
source_units.text: “You need not search here; it has been taken care of.”

source_units.text_ar: وَلَا يَلْقَى أَحَدًا إِلَّا رَدَّهُ وَوَفَى لَنَا» .
source_units.kind_ar: خبر أبي بكر: الوفاء برد الطلب
source_units.text: He turned back everyone he met and kept his word to us.”

source_units.text_ar: قال عبد الملك: فبلغنا أن أم معبد هاجرت إلى النبيّ، - ﷺ -، وأسلمت، وكان خروج رسول الله، - ﷺ -، من الغار ليلة الاثنين لأربع ليال خلون من شهر ربيع الأوّل فقال يوم الثلاثاء بقُديد (^٢)، فلمّا راحوا منها عرض لهم سُراقة بن مالك بن جُعشم وهو على فرس له، فدعا عليه رسول الله، - ﷺ -، فرسخت قوائم فرسه، فقال: يا محمّد ادعُ الله أن يطلق فرسي وأرجع عنك وأردّ من ورائي، ففعل، فأطلق ورجع فوجد النّاس يلتمسون رسول الله، - ﷺ -، فقال: ارجعوا فقد استبرأت لكم ما ههنا وقد عرفتم بصرى بالأثر، فرجعوا عنه.
source_units.speaker_ar: عبد الملك كما يسميه المصدر؛ سياق الطريق السابق
source_units.text: ‘Abd al-Malik said: We were told that Umm Ma‘bad migrated to the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left the cave on Monday night, four nights into the month of Rabi‘ al-Awwal, and arrived at Qudayd on Tuesday. When they departed from there, Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum came upon them on his horse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed against him, and the horse’s legs sank into the ground. He said, “Muhammad, pray to Allah to free my horse, and I will turn back from you and turn away those behind me.” He did so, and the horse was freed. Suraqah went back and found the people searching for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, “Go back. I have searched thoroughly for you in this area, and you know how good I am at tracking.” So they turned back.

source_units.text_ar: حَتَّى إذَا كَانَ فَتْحُ مَكَّةَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَفَرَغَ مِنْ حُنَيْنٍ وَالطَّائِفِ، خَرَجْتُ وَمَعِي الْكِتَابَ لَأَلْقَاهُ، فَلَقِيتُهُ بِالْجِعْرَانَةِ [٣] . قَالَ: فَدَخَلْتُ فِي كَتِيبَةٍ مِنْ خَيْلِ الْأَنْصَارِ. قَالَ: فَجَعَلُوا يَقْرَعُونَنِي بِالرِّمَاحِ وَيَقُولُونَ: إلَيْكَ (إلَيْكَ) [١]، مَاذَا تُرِيدُ؟ قَالَ: فَدَنَوْتُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَهُوَ عَلَى نَاقَتِهِ، وَاَللَّهِ لَكَأَنِّي أَنْظُرُ إلَى سَاقِهِ فِي غَرْزِهِ [٤] كَأَنَّهَا جُمَّارَةٌ. قَالَ: فَرَفَعْتُ يَدِي بِالْكِتَابِ، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، هَذَا كِتَابُكَ (لِي) [١]، أَنَا سُرَاقَةُ بْنُ جُعْشُمٍ، قَالَ: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ:
source_units.kind_ar: لقاء لاحق بعد الفتح وحنين والطائف
source_units.text: When the conquest of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he had finished with Hunayn and al-Taif, I went out with the letter to meet him, and met him at al-Ji‘ranah [٣]. He said: I entered a troop of the Ansar’s cavalry. They began striking me with their spears and saying, “Back! (Back!) [١] What do you want?” He said: I approached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was on his she-camel. By Allah, I can almost see his shin in the stirrup [٤], like the white inner core of a palm shoot. He said: I raised my hand holding the letter and said, “Messenger of Allah, this is your letter (to me) [١]. I am Suraqa ibn Ju‘shum.” He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

source_units.text_ar: يَوْمُ وَفَاءٍ وَبِرٍّ، ادْنُهْ.
source_units.text: “A day of fidelity and kindness. Bring him near.”

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَ:
فَدَنَوْتُ مِنْهُ، فَأَسْلَمْتُ. ثُمَّ تَذَكَّرْتُ شَيْئًا أَسْأَلُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَنْهُ فَمَا أَذْكُرُهُ، إلَّا أَنِّي قُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، الضَّالَّةُ مِنْ الْإِبِلِ تَغْشَى حِيَاضِي، وَقَدْ مَلَأْتهَا لِإِبِلِي، هَلْ لِي مِنْ أَجْرٍ فِي أَنْ أَسْقِيَهَا؟ قَالَ:
source_units.kind_ar: إسلام سراقة وسؤاله في اللقاء اللاحق
source_units.text:
He said:
I approached him and accepted Islam. Then I remembered something I wanted to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about, though I cannot recall it; I did say, “Messenger of Allah, stray camels come to my watering troughs, which I have filled for my own camels. Is there a reward for me in giving them water?” He said:

source_units.text_ar:
وأَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْحُسَيْنِ بْنُ الْفَضْلِ الْقَطَّانُ بِبَغْدَادَ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو بكر محمد ابْنَ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَتَّابٍ الْعَبْدِيُّ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ، قَالَ:
أَخْبَرَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي أُوَيْسٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ، عَنْ عَمِّهِ مُوسَى بْنِ عُقْبَةَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ شِهَابٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ ابن مَالِكِ بْنِ جُعْشُمٍ الْمُدْلِجِيُّ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ مَالِكًا أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ أَخَاهَ سُرَاقَةَ بْنَ جُعْشُمٍ أَخْبَرَهُ:
«أَنَّهُ لَمَّا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ مِنْ مَكَّةَ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ جَعَلَتْ قُرَيْشٌ لِمَنْ رَدَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِائَةَ نَاقَةٍ قَالَ: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا جَالِسٌ فِي نَادِي قَوْمِي إِذْ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ مِنَّا فَقَالَ: وَاللهِ لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ رَكْبًا ثَلَاثَةً مَرُّوا عَلَيَّ آنِفًا، إِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ مُحَمَّدًا، قَالَ:
فَأَوْمَأْتُ إِلَيْهِ بِعَيْنَيَّ: أَنِ اسْكُتْ، وَقُلْتُ: إِنَّمَا هُمْ بَنُو فُلَانَ يَبْتَغُونَ ضالة
source_units.speaker_ar: سراقة بن مالك؛ وابن شهاب في موضع السؤال
source_units.text:
Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Qattan in Baghdad informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Attab al-‘Abdi informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn ‘Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah told us, saying:
Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways informed us, saying: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim ibn ‘Uqbah told me, from his uncle Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, who said: Ibn Shihab told us, saying: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum al-Mudliji told me that his father Malik had informed him that his brother Suraqah ibn Ju‘shum had informed him:
“When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Makkah as a migrant to Madinah, Quraysh offered one hundred she-camels to anyone who brought him back to them. He said: While I was sitting in the gathering place of my people, a man from among us came and said, ‘By Allah, I have just seen three riders pass by me. I think it was Muhammad.’ He said:

source_units.text_ar:
لَهُمْ، قَالَ: لَعَلَّهُ، ثُمَّ سَكَتَ.
قَالَ: فَمَكَثْتُ قَلِيلًا، ثُمَّ قُمْتُ فَدَخَلْتُ بَيْتِي وَأَمَرْتُ بِفَرَسِي، فَقُيِّدَ إِلَى بَطْنِ الْوَادِي، وَأَخْرَجْتُ سِلَاحِي مِنْ وَرَاءِ حُجُرَاتِي، ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُ قَدَاحِي أَسْتَقْسِمُ بِهَا، ثُمَّ لَبِسْتُ لَأْمَتِي، ثُمَّ أَخْرَجَتُ قَدَاحِي فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِهَا، فَخَرَجَ السَّهْمُ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ: لَا تَضُرُّهُ، وَكُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ أَرُدَّهُ فَآخُذَ الْمِائَةَ نَاقَةٍ.
قَالَ: فَرَكِبْتُ عَلَى أَثَرِهِ، فَبَيْنَا فَرَسِي يَسِيرُ بِي عَثَرَ، فَسَقَطْتُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ: فَأَخْرَجَتُ قَدَاحِي فَاسْتَقْسَمْتُ بِهَا فَخَرَجَ السَّهْمُ الَّذِي أَكْرَهُ: لَا تَضُرُّهُ، فَأَبَيْتُ إِلَّا أَنْ أَتْبَعَهُ، فَرَكِبْتُ، فَلَمَّا بَدَا لِي الْقَوْمُ فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهِمْ عَثَرَ بِي فَرَسِي فَذَهَبَتْ يَدَاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ، فَسَقَطْتُ عَنْهُ، فَاسْتَخْرَجَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَتْبَعْهُمَا دُخَانٌ مِثْلَ الْغُبَارِ، فَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ مُنِعَ مِنِّي، وَأَنَّهُ ظَاهِرٌ، فناديتهم، فقلت: انظروني فو الله لَا آذَيْتُكُمْ، وَلَا يَأْتِيكُمْ مِنِّي شَيْءٌ تَكْرَهُونَهُ.
فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌: قُلْ لَهُ: مَاذَا تَبْتَغِي؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ اكْتُبْ لِي كِتَابًا يَكُونُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ آيَةً، قَالَ: اكْتُبْ لَهُ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، قَالَ: فَكَتَبَ لِي ثُمَّ أَلْقَاهُ إِلَيَّ، فَرَجَعْتُ، فَسَكَتُّ، فَلَمْ أَذْكُرْ شَيْئًا مِمَّا كَانَ، حَتَّى إِذَا فَتَحَ اللهُ ﷿ مَكَّةَ، وَفَرَغَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ مِنْ أَهْلِ خَيْبَرَ، خَرَجْتُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ ﵌ لِأَلْقَاهُ وَمَعِي الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي كَتَبَ لِي، فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا عَامِدٌ لَهُ دَخَلْتُ بَيْنَ ظَهْرَيْ كَتِيبَةٍ مِنْ كَتَائِبِ الْأَنْصَارِ، قَالَ: فَطَفِقُوا يَقْرَعُونَنِي بِالرِّمَاحِ، وَيَقُولُونَ: إِلَيْكَ، إِلَيْكَ، حَتَّى دَنَوْتُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﵌ وَهُوَ عَلَى نَاقَتِهِ أَنْظُرُ إِلَى سَاقِهِ فِي غَرْزِهِ، كَأَنَّهَا جُمَّارَةٌ، فَرَفَعْتُ يَدِي بِالْكِتَابِ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ! هَذَا كِتَابُكَ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌: يَوْمُ وَفَاءٍ وَبِرٍّ، ادْنُهُ، قَالَ: فَأَسْلَمْتُ،
ثُمَّ ذَكَرْتُ شَيْئًا أَسَلُ عَنْهُ رَسُولَ اللهِ ﵌.
قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ: إِنَّمَا سَأَلَهُ عَنِ الضَّالَّةِ، وَشَيْءٍ فَعَلَهُ فِي وَجْهِهِ الَّذِي كَانَ فِيهِ، فَمَا ذَكَرْتُ شَيْئًا إِلَّا أَنِّي قَدْ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ: الضَّالَّةُ تَغْشَى حِيَاضِي قَدْ
source_units.speaker_ar: سراقة بن مالك؛ وابن شهاب في موضع السؤال
source_units.text:
“I signaled to him with my eyes to be quiet, and said, ‘They are only so-and-so’s people, looking for a lost animal.’ He said, ‘Perhaps,’ and then fell silent.
He said: I stayed a little while, then got up and went into my house. I ordered my horse to be brought; it was tethered at the bottom of the valley. I took my weapons from behind my living quarters, then took my divining arrows and drew lots with them. I put on my armor, then brought out the arrows and drew lots again. The arrow I disliked came up: ‘He will not be harmed.’ Yet I hoped to bring him back and take the hundred she-camels.
He said: I mounted and followed his tracks. While my horse was carrying me along, it stumbled and I fell off. I brought out my arrows and drew lots again, and the arrow I disliked came up: ‘He will not be harmed.’ But I insisted on pursuing him, so I mounted. When the group came into view and I saw them, my horse stumbled; its forelegs sank into the ground, and I fell off. It pulled its forelegs free, and smoke like dust trailed after them. Then I knew that he had been protected from me and that he would prevail. I called out to them and said, ‘Wait for me! By Allah, I will not harm you, and nothing you dislike will come from me.’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘Ask him what he wants.’ I said, ‘Write me a document that will be a token between us.’ He said, ‘Write one for him, Abu Bakr.’ He wrote it for me and tossed it to me. I went back and kept quiet; I did not mention anything that had happened. When Allah, mighty and majestic is He, opened Makkah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished with the people of Khaybar, I set out to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, carrying the document he had written for me. As I was making my way to him, I entered among a company of the Ansar. They began prodding me with their spears, saying, ‘Move along, move along,’ until I drew near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was on his she-camel. I could see his leg in the stirrup, like a date-palm pith. I raised the document in my hand and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, this is your document.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘A day of fulfillment and kindness. Bring him near.’ He said: Then I accepted Islam.
Then I mentioned something I wanted to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about.
Ibn Shihab said: He had only asked him about the lost animals and something he had done to him when they were in that situation. I mentioned nothing except that I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, lost animals come to my watering troughs ...’”

source_units.text_ar: وسأل سراقة أن يكتب له رسول اللَّه ﷺ كتابا، فكتب له أبو بكر ﵁، ويقال: بل كتب له عامر بن فهيرة، في أديم [(١)] ورجع يقول للناس: قد كفيتم ما هاهنا، ويرد عنهم الطلب.
source_units.book_ar: إمتاع الأسماع بما للنبي من الأحوال والأموال والحفدة والمتاع
source_units.citation_ar: [إمتاع الأسماع بما للنبي من الأحوال والأموال والحفدة والمتاع، 1/60](https://app.turath.io/book/1524?page=99)
source_units.text: Suraqah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to write him a document. Abu Bakr wrote it for him, though it is said that ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah wrote it for him, on a piece of leather. He then returned, telling people, “You have no need to search here,” and turning the pursuit away from them.

source_units.text_ar: (قوله ابن فهيرة) بضم الفاء وفتح الهاء وسكون المثناة التحتية قيل كتابه ﷺ نيف وأربعون = = وأكثرهم ملازمة له زَيْد بن ثَابت ومعاوية بن أبى سفيان بعد الفتح وقيل أبو بكر، وجمع بين القولين بأن ابن فهيرة كتب أولا وكتب الصديق آخرا (*)
source_units.speaker_ar: الشمني في الحاشية؛ قيل وجمع بلا تسمية قائل الجمع
source_units.book_ar: الشفا بتعريف حقوق المصطفى - وحاشية الشمني
source_units.text: (The phrase “Ibn Fuhayrah”): The fā’ has a dammah, the hā’ a fatḥah, and the yā’ is still. It is said that he ﷺ had more than forty scribes. The two who kept his company most closely were Zayd ibn Thābit and Mu‘āwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān after the Conquest; it is also said that it was Abu Bakr. The two reports can be reconciled by saying that Ibn Fuhayrah wrote first and the Truthful One wrote later.

source_units.text_ar:
أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو الْحُسَيْنِ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ الْقَطَّانُ بِبَغْدَادَ، وقَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّه بْنُ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ دُرُسْتَوَيْهِ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ سُفْيَانَ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّه بْنُ مُوسَى، وَعَبْدُ اللَّه بْنُ رَجَاءٍ: أَبُو عُمَرَ الْغُدَانِيُّ، عَنْ إِسْرَائِيلَ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ، قَالَ: «اشْتَرَى أَبُو بَكْرٍ مِنْ عَازِبٍ رَحْلًا بِثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ دِرْهَمًا، فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁ لِعَازِبٍ: مُرِ الْبَرَاءَ فَلْيَحْمِلْهُ إِلَى رَحْلِي، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَازِبٌ: لَا، حَتَّى تُحَدِّثَنَا كَيْفَ صَنَعْتَ أَنْتَ وَرَسُولُ اللَّه ﵌ حِينَ خَرَجْتُمَا وَالْمُشْرِكُونَ يَطْلُبُونَكُمَا قَالَ: أَدْلَجْنَا مِنْ مَكَّةَ لَيْلًا، فَأَحْيَيْنَا لَيْلَتَنَا وَيَوْمَنَا حَتَّى أَظْهَرْنَا، وَقَامَ قَائِمُ الظَّهِيرَةِ، فَرَمَيْتُ بِبَصَرِي هَلْ أَرَى مِنْ ظِلٍّ نَأْوِي إِلَيْهِ فَإِذَا صَخْرَةٌ، فَانْتَهَيْتُ إِلَيْهَا، فَإِذَا بَقِيَّةُ ظِلٍّ لَهَا، فَسَوَّيْتُهُ، ثُمَّ فَرَشْتُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّه ﵌ فَرْوَةً، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: اضْطَجِعْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّه، فَاضْطَجَعَ، ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ أَنْفُضُ مَا حَوْلِي هَلْ أَرَى مِنَ الطَّلَبِ أَحَدًا، فَإِذَا بِرَاعِي غَنَمٍ يَسُوقُ غَنَمَهُ إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ يُرِيدُ مِنْهَا الَّذِي نُرِيدُ- يَعْنِي الظِّلَّ- فَسَأَلْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ: لِمَنْ أَنْتَ يَا غُلَامُ؟ فَقَالَ: لِرَجُلٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، فَسَمَّاهُ، فَعَرَفْتُهُ، فَقُلْتُ: هَلْ فِي غَنَمِكَ مِنْ لَبَنٍ، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، قُلْتُ:
هَلْ أَنْتَ حَالِبٌ لِي، قَالَ: نَعَمْ، فَأَمَرْتُهُ فَاعْتَقَلَ شَاةً مِنْ غَنَمِهِ، وَأَمَرْتُهُ أَنْ يَنْفُضَ ضَرْعَهَا مِنَ التُّرَابِ، ثُمَّ أَمَرْتُهُ أَنْ يَنْفُضَ كَفَّيْهِ، فَقَالَ: هَكَذَا، فَضَرَبَ إِحْدَى كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى الْأُخْرَى، فَحَلَبَ لِي كُثْبَةً [(١)] مِنْ لَبَنٍ وَقَدْ رَوَيْتُ مَعِي لِرَسُولِ اللَّه
source_units.text: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan in Baghdad informed us, saying: ‘Abdullah ibn Ja‘far ibn Durustawayh informed us, saying: Ya‘qub ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: ‘Ubaydullah ibn Musa and ‘Abdullah ibn Raja’, Abu ‘Umar al-Ghudani, narrated to us, from Isra’il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara’, who said: “Abu Bakr bought a saddle from ‘Azib for thirteen dirhams. Abu Bakr said to ‘Azib: ‘Tell al-Bara’ to carry it to my saddle.’ ‘Azib said to him: ‘No, not until you tell us what you and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did when you set out and the polytheists were pursuing you.’ He said: ‘We left Makkah at night and traveled through the night and the day until the afternoon. When the midday heat set in, I looked around to see whether there was any shade where we could take shelter. I saw a rock and went to it. There was a patch of shade beside it, so I leveled it. Then I spread a fur for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “Lie down, Messenger of Allah.” He lay down. Then I went off, looking around me to see whether I could spot any pursuers. Suddenly I saw a shepherd driving his sheep toward the rock, seeking the same thing we were—the shade. I asked him, “Whose shepherd are you, young man?” He said, “A man from Quraysh,” and named him. I recognized the man and asked, “Do any of your sheep have milk?” He said, “Yes.” I asked, “Will you milk one for me?” He said, “Yes.” I told him to catch a sheep from his flock and shake the dust from its udder. Then I told him to shake his hands. He said, “Like this?” and struck one hand against the other. He milked a small amount of milk for me. I had brought a water-skin for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with a cloth over its opening. I poured water over the milk until the bottom of the container was cool. Then I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that he had woken up. I said, “Will you drink, Messenger of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ drank until I was satisfied. Then I said, “It is time to set out, Messenger of Allah.”’

“Will you wear the bracelets of Kisra?”

During the caliphate of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, when the cities were conquered, Kisra’s two bracelets were brought to ‘Umar. He summoned Suraqah ibn Malik, put them on him, and said, “Raise your hands.” Suraqah said, “Allah is the Greatest. Praise be to Allah, who took them from Kisra ibn Hurmuz—the one who used to say, ‘I am the lord of people’—and placed them on Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum, a Bedouin from Banu Mudlij.”

The hadith scholar included this report in *al-Isabah*, and Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr included it in *al-Isti‘ab*, with a broken chain of transmission.

I say: It is established that Kisra’s treasures were brought to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab. Al-Baghawi related in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, with an authentic chain of transmission, from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, who said: When Kisra’s treasures were brought to ‘Umar, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Arqam al-Zuhri said to him, “Will you not put them in the treasury until you distribute them?”

questions.prompt: Quraysh offered a reward for the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr. What did Suraqah hope to do?

options.text: Tell Quraysh which way the Prophet ﷺ had gone
options.feedback: He wanted more than to pass on news: he meant to bring the Prophet ﷺ back himself and claim the reward.

options.text: Bring the Prophet ﷺ back to Quraysh and take the hundred she-camels
options.feedback: Right. Suraqah said so himself: "I hoped to bring him back to Quraysh and take the hundred she-camels."

options.text: Lead his whole tribe out and share the reward with them
options.feedback: He did the opposite: he hid what he knew from his tribe so that the reward would be his alone.

questions.explanation: The price on the travellers' heads drew Suraqah into the chase; he hoped to bring the Prophet ﷺ back and win a hundred she-camels.

questions.prompt: A man of Banu Mudlij said he had seen dark figures by the coast. What did Suraqah tell him?

options.text: That they were other people, though he knew they were the Prophet ﷺ and his companions
options.feedback: Right. "I knew that it was them," Suraqah said, but he told the man he had seen so-and-so, who had set out before their eyes.

options.text: That he was right, and they should ride out together at once
options.feedback: Suraqah agreed with no one and asked no one along. He kept his knowledge to himself so he could go alone.

options.text: That they were the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, and he would go after them
options.feedback: He announced nothing. He sat on in the gathering for a while, then slipped out by the back of his house.

questions.explanation: Suraqah recognised the riders at once but denied it aloud: he meant to catch them himself.

questions.prompt: As Suraqah drew near, his horse stumbled and his arrows gave the answer he hated. What did he do next?

options.text: He gave up and rode home to his people
options.feedback: Not yet. He turned back only later, after his horse had sunk into the ground and he had spoken with the travellers.

options.text: He cast the arrows again and called out to ask for safety
options.feedback: That came later, after his horse's forelegs sank into the earth. At this first fall he was still set on the chase.

options.text: He mounted again, defying the arrows, and rode on
options.feedback: Right. He ignored the arrows and rode on until he could hear the Prophet ﷺ reciting.

questions.explanation: Neither the fall nor the arrows stopped Suraqah the first time; he defied them and closed in on the travellers.

questions.prompt: When the horseman was two or three spear-lengths away, Abu Bakr wept. Why did he say he was weeping?

options.text: He feared for his own life
options.feedback: He said the opposite: "By Allah, it is not for myself that I weep."

options.text: He feared for the Prophet ﷺ
options.feedback: Right. "It is not for myself that I weep," Abu Bakr said, "but for you." The Prophet ﷺ then prayed, "O Allah, suffice us however You will."

options.text: He had left his family behind in Makkah
options.feedback: His words were about the danger in front of them: "it is not for myself that I weep, but for you."

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr's fear was for the Prophet ﷺ, who answered it with calm ("Allah is with us") and with prayer.

questions.prompt: After his horse sank into the earth and he was held back from them, what came into Suraqah's mind?

options.text: That the cause of the Prophet ﷺ would prevail
options.feedback: Right. Being held back from them, he said, made him think the Prophet's ﷺ cause would prevail, and he asked for safety.

options.text: That he must try once more to win the reward
options.feedback: He gave up the chase instead: he called out for safety and rode up to them as a friend.

options.text: That he had been following the wrong riders
options.feedback: He never doubted who they were. It was what happened to his horse that changed his mind.

questions.explanation: The horse sinking turned the hunter around: Suraqah saw that the Prophet's ﷺ cause would prevail.

questions.prompt: Suraqah offered the travellers provisions and goods. What did the Prophet ﷺ ask of him?

options.text: To guide them on the road to Madinah
options.feedback: He asked for no guide. He asked only for silence.

options.text: To give them an arrow and take what they needed from his herds
options.feedback: That was Suraqah's offer, not their request. "We have no need of your camels and sheep," the Prophet ﷺ said.

options.text: To keep their whereabouts hidden
options.feedback: Right. "They took nothing from me and asked nothing of me," Suraqah said, "except that he said: 'Keep our whereabouts hidden.'"

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ refused Suraqah's goods and asked one thing of him: to keep their whereabouts hidden.

questions.prompt: What did Suraqah do on his way home after meeting the travellers?

options.text: He turned back every searcher he met, telling them the ground was already searched
options.feedback: Right. "He did not meet anyone without turning him back," Abu Bakr said, "and he kept his word to us."

options.text: He showed the searchers his letter of safety as proof
options.feedback: He told no one what had passed between them. He kept the letter for years, until al-Ji‘ranah.

options.text: He told Quraysh where he had met the travellers
options.feedback: That would have broken his word. He sent pursuers home instead: "You have been spared the search here."

questions.explanation: The hunter became a shield: Suraqah used his name as a tracker to send every pursuer home.

questions.prompt: Suraqah and Abu Bakr both told how the horse sank. How do their accounts differ?

options.text: Suraqah says it sank to its belly; Abu Bakr, its forelegs to the knees
options.feedback: This swaps them. Suraqah speaks of the forelegs to the knees; Abu Bakr of the horse sinking to its belly.

options.text: Suraqah says its forelegs sank to the knees; Abu Bakr, that it sank to its belly
options.feedback: Right. The two men saw the moment from opposite ends, and each is told as he gave it.

options.text: Suraqah says it stumbled twice; Abu Bakr, that it stumbled once
options.feedback: Two stumbles belong to Ibn Ishaq's telling of Suraqah's story, not to Abu Bakr's account.

questions.explanation: The pursuer and the pursued remember the same moment differently: to the knees for Suraqah, to the belly for Abu Bakr.

questions.prompt: Who wrote Suraqah's letter of safety, and on what, in al-Bukhari and in Ibn Ishaq?

options.text: Al-Bukhari: Abu Bakr, on leather; Ibn Ishaq: ‘Amir, on a bone, scrap or potsherd
options.feedback: The materials are right but the writers are swapped: al-Bukhari names ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Ibn Ishaq names Abu Bakr.

options.text: Al-Bukhari: ‘Amir, on a bone, scrap or potsherd; Ibn Ishaq: Abu Bakr, on leather
options.feedback: The writers are right but the materials are swapped: leather is al-Bukhari's, the bone, scrap or potsherd Ibn Ishaq's.

options.text: Al-Bukhari: ‘Amir, on leather; Ibn Ishaq: Abu Bakr, on a bone, scrap or potsherd
options.feedback: Right. Al-Maqrizi gives both names, and a note on al-Shifa reports that ‘Amir wrote first and Abu Bakr afterwards.

questions.explanation: The writer of the letter is a known difference: ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah on leather in al-Bukhari, Abu Bakr on a bone, scrap or potsherd in Ibn Ishaq.

questions.prompt: Suraqah swore "la-u‘ammiyanna" the tullab, "I will blind the pursuers." What did he mean?

options.text: He would hide the travellers from those searching for them
options.feedback: Right. Isma‘il al-Isbahani explains it as "I will hide you from them", and Suraqah did so, turning every searcher back.

options.text: He would ask Allah to strike the pursuers blind
options.feedback: He was the one asking for prayer, to be freed from the sinking ground. The blinding was his promise of concealment.

options.text: He would lead the pursuers off in the wrong direction by night
options.feedback: The word means hiding the travellers from them, not leading anyone on a false trail.

questions.explanation: "I will blind them" was Suraqah's promise to hide the travellers; tullab can mean one pursuer or many.
